rv.q: Urgent and affecting, if heavy-handed climate-change drama
This play is too keen to make its case (and has too many cases to make) for it to succeed as it might, were it to let the characters breathe a little, underwater or otherwise.

I think the show is necessary viewing for all generations to remind us of the culture of protest that we have as a country and how we need to make sure that it is not lost as we fight back against one of the gravest threats that humanity has ever faced in our history.
Emily White’s new play is engaging, amusing, and thought provoking, only occasionally veering into the hectoring lecture protest style of delivery.

cn.t: This Welsh-set drama divides critics, earning praise for its engaging, thought-provoking examination of society while others find it less successful, though most appreciate White's ambitious storytelling.
